_comment: Failures recorded so the suite fails on NEW regressions rather than on an
existing backlog. Remove an id when its bug is fixed — the runner reports
an entry that starts passing, so this list cannot rot silently.
unmodelled_kind: DBDiff produces NO diff while the schemas genuinely
differ, because it does not model that object kind at all. These are
feature gaps, and the more dangerous class: a user sees 'no drift' and
Empty since composite types, domains, materialised views, RLS policies
and standalone sequences became modelled kinds: all five now diff, and
the DDL they emit round-trips through the server on PG 14-18.
wrong_output: DBDiff produces a diff, but applying it does not reproduce
the target schema. These are defects in existing behaviour.

alter_path: failures on ALTER patterns, invisible until the regression source was fixed. The suite had been fetching 404s and testing object creation only. The identity ones went once identity changes were made in place (#236).

hard_cases: the renderer corpus from @akalforge/pg-conformance, now run in CI. These are DDL shapes the renderer cannot yet reproduce — exclusion constraints, NULLS NOT DISTINCT, NOT VALID, foreign key variants and several partitioning forms. Recorded so the count can only go down.

builtin_renderer_only: cases pg_dump reproduces on PostgreSQL 16-18 and the built-in renderer does not yet. Known failures only on a run that never used pg_dump (none on PATH, too old, or DBDIFF_PG_DUMP_RENDERER=off); CI installs a matching pg_dump, so there they must pass.
